topic: Ethics: Ethical Theories (Natural Law, Situation Ethics, Virtue Ethics)
subject: religious-studies

items.title: Natural Law has primary and secondary precepts
items.claim: What are Aquinas's primary precepts of natural law?

options.text: Five primary precepts identified by Aquinas: preservation of life, reproduction, education of offspring, living in society, worship of God — secondary precepts (specific moral rules) are derived from them by reason
A single rule: do good and avoid evil

items.reveal:
Aquinas's natural law theory appears in the Summa Theologiae I-II (Questions 90-97). The eternal law is God's plan; natural law is rational creatures' participation in it; human law derives specific rules.

The doctrine of double effect — an action with a foreseen bad consequence can be permissible if the bad effect is not intended, the act itself is not intrinsically wrong, and the good outweighs the bad — is a key application (used in modern bioethics).

Natural law is the basis of Catholic moral teaching on contraception, abortion and end-of-life care. John Finnis and Germain Grisez developed 'New Natural Law' (from 1980) updating the framework.
items.why: Catholic ethics is not arbitrary doctrine — it rests on a developed rational framework. Engaging with natural law requires understanding the structure (primary, secondary, double effect) rather than treating it as a list of forbidden actions.

items.title: Aristotelian virtue ethics aims at eudaimonia, not just being virtuous
items.claim: What is eudaimonia in Aristotle's ethics?

options.text: Flourishing or living well — the proper end of human life. The virtues (excellences of character) are dispositions that enable a person to function well as a human being and so to live a flourishing life

items.reveal:
Aristotle's 'Nicomachean Ethics' (Book I) argues that all human action aims at some good, and there must be a highest good — eudaimonia.

The ergon (function) argument: humans, like everything, have a characteristic function — rational activity according to virtue. The virtues are not lists of good behaviours but stable dispositions developed through habituation.

The doctrine of the mean: each virtue is between two vices (courage between cowardice and recklessness; generosity between miserliness and profligacy).

Alasdair MacIntyre's 'After Virtue' (1981) revived virtue ethics by arguing that modern moral discourse has lost the framework that gives moral vocabulary its meaning.
items.why: Virtue ethics is not 'be a good person'. It is a structured theory with specific terms — function, habituation, the mean, flourishing — that link character to the good life in a way that act-based theories don't.
